chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, who traces it up to Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, concerning:
Pure khazz—there is no harm in it. But as for that in which rabbit fur or other such similar things are mixed, one should not perform salat (prayer) in it.

key_terms.الْخَزِّ: khazz, a type of fabric discussed in rulings of salat (prayer) dress
key_terms.فَلَا يُصَلِّي: then one should not perform salat (prayer)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; it is permissible
key_terms.وَبَرُ الْأَرَانِبِ: rabbit fur used as a mixed material

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform salat (prayer) in mixed khazz fabric containing rabbit fur?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding performing salat (prayer) in garments made of khazz. Pure khazz is permitted, but khazz mixed with rabbit fur or similar materials is not to be worn in salat (prayer).
